business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stevedoring and Loading/Unloading of Bulk Cargo at Marine Docks

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Free Trade Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, adopted 29 December 2023, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 4, 10-11, 23-33, 46-47, 59-63, 68 and 83; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4, 12, 28-34; Regulations for Implementing the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (State Council Decree No. 723, 2020), Articles 5-15; Measures for the Administration of Port Operation Permits (Ministry of Transport).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Market Entity Registration of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), delegated to the local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation at the company's registered address, operating through the National Enterprise Integrated Registration Platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, accompanied by the Articles of Association, the Foreign Investment Information Report and the Name Pre-Approval Notice.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under national law. No minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement applies to a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise limited liability company under the Company Law of the PRC. Shareholders must subscribe to the registered capital in the Articles of Association and pay the subscribed capital within five years from the date of establishment unless a shorter or longer period is otherwise prescribed by law. For a port stevedoring terminal, the port licensing authority may assess financial capability and projected capital expenditure as part of the Port Operation License application, but this is not an escrow or blocked-account requirement. Paid-in capital is credited to the company's capital account maintained at a licensed bank and may be applied to lawful business purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [INSERT COMPLETE COMPANY NAME] WFOE LIMITED, CHINA

RECITALS
WHEREAS the shareholders of the Company have resolved to incorporate and operate the Company as a limited liability company wholly owned by foreign investors under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China; and
WHEREAS the business scope of the Company includes maritime cargo handling, stevedoring and loading/unloading of bulk cargo at a port terminal, and ancillary port logistics services; and
WHEREAS the Company requires, as a matter of law and good corporate governance, an adopted share-capital structure, authorized banking arrangements, a statutory registered office, and duly appointed statutory officers before applying for the Port Operation License and undertaking industrial operations.

NOW THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AND RECORDED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The registered capital of the Company as specified in the Articles of Association is hereby ratified and adopted. The authorized officers of the Company are directed to record each shareholder's subscription in the share ledger, to monitor contribution schedules, and to ensure that all cash and in-kind contributions are received or transferred in accordance with the Articles of Association and within the statutory contribution period. No share certificate shall be issued until the relevant contribution is fully made, unless a later issuance is explicitly authorized by applicable law.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Bank of China branch designated by the Board is approved as the principal settlement bank. The Chairman and the General Manager, acting either jointly or with the Financial Officer, are hereby authorized to open RMB and foreign-currency bank accounts, sign all account opening application forms, execute online banking agreements, set transaction limits, and maintain the authorized signatory list for the Company.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company is adopted as [Full Registered Address], which shall be stated in the Business License, in all contracts, and in all statutory filings. The authorized officers are directed to execute the lease agreement, pay rent and deposits, and maintain the registered office for receipt of legal process and official correspondence.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The following individuals are appointed with immediate effect upon completion of incorporation: Director and Chairman of the Board; General Manager; Legal Representative; and Supervisor or Supervisors as required by law. The Legal Representative and General Manager are jointly and severally authorized, within their respective borders, to execute registration forms, tax registrations, labor and social insurance filings, bank documents, seal applications, and port licensing applications.

5. AUTHORITY AND EFFECT. All officers and agents of the Company are authorized to do any act and execute any document necessary to implement this resolution. This resolution is effective upon adoption and remains in force until amended or revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board. A certified extract of this resolution, bearing the Company seal and Legal Representative's signature, may be relied upon by any government authority, bank, registrar or counterparty as conclusive evidence of the authorities granted herein.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Registration and Foreign Investor Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration System and local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation; foreign investment negative-list consultation is embedded in the integrated registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit one proposed company name containing the entity type 'WFOE Limited Liability Company' through the SAMR online enterprise-name registration module. In the business-scope field, enter the verbatim scope 'cargo handling and stevedoring at maritime ports, bulk cargo loading and unloading, port logistics and ancillary port services.' The system automatically checks name conflicts with prior registered enterprises and protected marks. The applicant must confirm that the proposed business is outside the Foreign Investment Negative List. If the name is rejected, the case handler will issue a rejection reason and the applicant may resubmit a revised name. Once the name is approved, it is reserved for a statutory period.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of foreign investor's certificate of incorporation or passport
Power of attorney for formation agent
Proof of intended registered office or landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, amend and resubmit the name application within the appeal window; if the system flags a negative-list item, revise the business scope to exclude the restricted activity or restructure through a permissible licensed joint venture and consult the local commerce authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization of Foreign Investor Documents and Foreign Investment Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) Foreign Investment Information Reporting module, integrated with the SAMR registration system; consular legalization or apostille channel for foreign-issued documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before formal company registration, compile and legalize the foreign constitutional pack. Foreign investor corporate resolutions, identity certificates and powers of attorney issued outside China must be notarized in the country of origin and legalized by the Chinese consulate or apostilled under the applicable treaty if recognized by the PRC. Chinese translations must be attached to every foreign-language document. The Foreign Investment Information Report is filed through the integrated registration system and contains the investor nationality, ultimate beneficial owner, proposed business scope, registered capital and contribution period. The authority reviews compliance with the Foreign Investment Law and the Negative List and issues an information receipt. Discrepancies can be corrected in the same filing without restarting the application.
required_dossiers: Notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation of foreign investor
Notarized board or shareholders resolution of foreign investor approving the WFOE
Power of attorney for the formation agent
List of directors, supervisors and proposed legal representative with consent forms
Chinese translation certificate for each foreign language document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Foreign Investment Information Report is returned for an inconsistent beneficial owner declaration or negative-list mismatch, submit a corrected ownership declaration and revised business scope; an administrative reconsideration may be filed but does not suspend the correction deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation at the district level; free-trade-zone One-Stop Service Window if the terminal is located in a designated free trade zone.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company in person or through the integrated online registration portal. Attach the name pre-approval certificate, final Articles of Association, registered office lease and property ownership proof, legalized investor documents, appointment instruments, and identity documents of all directors, supervisors and the legal representative. The SAMR clerk will verify the registered office, review the proposed business scope, and confirm the governance structure complies with the Company Law. Once approved, the AMR issues the Business License with a unified social credit code, reflecting the establishment date and approved scope. The applicant must verify that the business license contains the operating item 'port cargo handling' together with the standard post-approval annotation requiring a port operation permit.
required_dossiers: Notarized Application for Establishment Registration signed by legal representative
Lease contract and property ownership certificate of registered office
Appointment and identity of directors, supervisors and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR issues an objection, respond within the statutory correction period with revised documents; if the business scope is ambiguous, amend the Articles of Association and resubmit; if the registered address is rejected, replace it with a compliant address and file a new landlord consent and lease deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Setup: Seals, Tax Registration, Social Insurance, Bank Accounts and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraving service; State Taxation Administration through shared registration data; Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; licensed commercial bank for the capital account; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through delegated banks.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Business License, formally adopt the First Board Resolution and appoint the bank mandate. Apply to a PSB-filed engraving shop to make the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal and invoice seal. SAMR data sharing automatically completes basic tax registration, but the legal representative must file tax form, accounting policy and general taxpayer forms with the local tax office. Simultaneously register with social insurance and housing fund administrations as an employer. Open a basic RMB deposit account and a foreign-currency capital account at the designated bank, and arrange capital remittance to that account. The bank will complete SAFE foreign exchange registration and issue the Foreign Exchange Business Registration Receipt. Capital may be used for lawful operating expenses after conversion under applicable current-account rules.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution on bank mandate and registered office
Bank forms and account mandate forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises enhanced due diligence due to the foreign corporate beneficial owner, provide the group structure chart, audited financial statements and source-of-funds confirmation; if SAFE rejects the registration, direct the bank to correct the entity registration and resubmit the capital inflow declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Publicity, Statutory Books and Employment Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; State Taxation Administration; Ministry of Commerce; local human resources and labor administration; local port authority for industrial pre-clearance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the applicable statutory period after incorporation, file the initial information disclosure on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, including shareholders, directors, supervisors, legal representative and registered capital. Prepare the statutory minute book, issue share certificates, maintain the shareholder register and record the First Board Resolution in the minute book. Record any paid-in capital in the accounting books and file the post-contribution Foreign Investment Information Report. If the terminal will employ workers, execute written labor contracts, file employment rules with the local labor authority, and complete workplace injury insurance registration. The corporate dossier is then ready for the separate industrial port licensing application.
required_dossiers: Share certificate stubs and shareholder register
Foreign investment information reports after capital contribution
National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System login and password
Employment contracts and labor filing forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a filing deadline is missed, submit a late report with the relevant explanatory letter; if the credit-information system blocks disclosure, present the hard-copy application with the corporate seal at the AMR window; an overdue annual report can be cured but may attract an admonition a temporary listing on the exceptional list until corrected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Transport (MOT) of the People's Republic of China, the local Harbor Administration or Port, Shipping and Logistics Administration, and the China Maritime Safety Administration for navigation and port facility security; the local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation is competent for special equipment registration and the local ecology bureau for environmental licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Port Operation License for Cargo Handling and Bulk Stevedoring (Port Operation Permit issued under the Port Law of the People's Republic of China), together with, if dangerous bulk goods are handled, a Dangerous Goods Port Operation Permit; an additional Pollutant Discharge Permit is required for the terminal operation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China, with implementation by the municipal or provincial Bureau of Ecology and Environment according to delegated thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report is required for a new or expanded bulk stevedoring terminal with berth capacity of 1,000 deadweight tonnes or above, or for any project located in an environmentally sensitive area. Medium projects may require an EIA Report Form, and small auxiliary installations with no sensitive receptors may be satisfied by an EIA Registration Record. Because bulk loading/unloading generates fugitive dust, vessel wastewater and noise, the project should be treated as a Class A Port and Shipping project requiring a full EIA Report. If the WFOE merely acquires an existing operating terminal without construction changes, an environmental change-of-operator filing and a new Pollutant Discharge Permit application may be required rather than a new construction EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: terminal domestic sewage and stormwater runoff must comply with the Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard GB 8978-1996, Grade III limits of COD 500 mg/L, suspended solids 400 mg/L, ammonia nitrogen 45 mg/L and petroleum oil 30 mg/L before discharge to municipal sewers; direct discharge to surface water is generally prohibited and, where exceptionally allowed, Grade I limits of COD 100 mg/L, suspended solids 70 mg/L and petroleum oil 5 mg/L apply. Vessel bilge water and ballast water must comply with GB 3552-2018, with oil content not exceeding 15 mg/L and no visible oil sheen. Air: fugitive particulate matter at the boundary must not exceed 1.0 mg/m3 and point-source dust emission concentration must not exceed 120 mg/m3 under GB 16297-1996. Bulk cargo transfer points must be enclosed, with dust-suppression systems using water spray or bag filters. If any ancillary fuel-storage or VOC-emitting equipment is installed, non-methane hydrocarbon outlet concentration must not exceed 120 mg/m3 and boundary fugitive concentration must not exceed 2.0 mg/m3. Hazardous waste: must be stored in a compliant hazardous-waste warehouse, shall not be stored for more than one year without an approved extension, and must be transferred only through the electronic manifest to a licensed hazardous-waste treatment facility in accordance with GB 18597-2023.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Air Defense (Civil Defense) construction approval is required for terminal fixed buildings and any personnel shelter area, as determined by the local civil air defense authority. Fire safety certification includes a fire protection design review and a completion fire safety acceptance certificate issued by the Fire and Rescue Department for all buildings, warehouses and vessel-berthing installations. Occupational and workplace safety clearance under the Work Safety Law requires a terminal safety assessment, a safety production responsibility system, emergency response plans, dust-control measures, and training records for stevedores and signalmen. Special equipment such as quay cranes, belt conveyors, mobile hoppers and forklifts must be inspected and registered with the municipal Market Regulation Administration before first use. The terminal must also carry an approved Port Facility Security Plan and appoint a Port Facility Security Officer in accordance with the ISPS Code and Chinese maritime safety regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online electronic portal: Electronic Tax Bureau (e-tax) national unified platform at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn, operating through provincial e-tax portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) with the local Market Regulation Administration (SAMR) as a foreign-invested limited liability company and obtain the Business License containing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for PRC tax purposes. Step 2: Complete post-issuance tax registration via the Electronic Tax Bureau, including confirmation of taxpayer details, tax types (CIT, VAT, stamp duty, etc.), filing frequency, bank account filing, and statutory bookkeeping requirements. Step 3: For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment or fixed base in China, file a separate non-resident enterprise tax registration through the withholding agent or directly with the STA using e-tax, and obtain a non-resident taxpayer code for EIT/VAT withholding. Step 4: Register in the VAT invoice management system and apply for e-invoice issuance quotas and digital invoice titles. Step 5: File foreign exchange receipts with SAFE through the designated settlement bank; no separate TIN is required for foreign exchange administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC tax system does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections for WFOEs. A WFOE is an entity-level CIT taxpayer on worldwide income; the only available VAT status election is small-scale taxpayer treatment for annual taxable turnover below RMB 5,000,000, which does not alter the entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT Law
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for VAT registration of a WFOE; registration is triggered by entity formation and taxable business activity. General VAT taxpayer status is mandatory when annual taxable services turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000; below that threshold, small-scale taxpayer status may apply at a 3% simplified levy rate (with temporary relief rates when lawfully announced).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The STA mandates issuance of all-digital electronic invoices (Su Dian Piao) through the national electronic invoice service platform, with real-time transmission of invoice data to the Golden Tax information system. Each invoice carries a unique invoice number and anti-counterfeit QR code; Special VAT Invoices require pre-approved quotas in the e-tax system and recipient verification through the national VAT invoice verification platform. The e-invoice platform exposes official interfaces/APIs for enterprise ERP reconciliation, and taxpayers must ensure that billing, clearing, and fiscal reporting are synchronized with the STA framework.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from China may be zero-rated/refunded under the export-tax refund system only when the exporter files a valid Export Goods Customs Declaration, the goods physically depart from mainland China, title passes to the overseas buyer, and the export proceeds are received and reported in accordance with SAFE rules. For the WFOE's stevedoring services at marine docks, 0% VAT is not available because loading/unloading of bulk cargo is physically performed in mainland China and is subject to VAT at 6% as a logistics auxiliary service. Qualifying cross-border services wholly consumed outside China may be zero-rated only if the invoice recipient is overseas, the service is in the statutory zero-rated catalogue, and documentary evidence proves performance and consumption outside China.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Original Export Goods Customs Declaration (export tax rebate special copy)
Ocean Bill of Lading or equivalent sea waybill evidencing outbound shipment
Foreign exchange proceeds receipt confirmation issued by the settlement bank under SAFE monitoring
Export sales contract and any amendments
Bulk cargo terminal operational evidence, including draft survey report, weight certificate, stevedoring tally sheet, and terminal handling charge records
Special VAT invoice or VAT special payment book substantiating the domestic purchase of export goods where refund is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating and export refund claims are subject to joint data cross-checks by the STA, General Administration of Customs, and SAFE. Failure to collect export proceeds within 180 days from customs declaration, or any mismatch among customs declarations, foreign exchange receipts, invoices, and bills of lading, triggers clawback of the refund/zero-rating benefit with daily late-payment surcharge at 0.05%, and administrative penalty of 0.5 to 5 times the evaded/refunded tax. Knowingly fraudulent export refund claims are punishable as criminal export-fraud under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, with imprisonment and fines; affected taxpayers are also downgraded in tax credit rating and suspended from facilitated export-refund processing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime administered by SAFE under the People's Bank of China. For current account items, including port stevedoring service revenue, foreign exchange conversion is generally permissible once legal identity, contract authenticity, commercial invoices, and bank verification procedures are completed. Capital account items, however, remain tightly controlled: all foreign direct investment injection requires FDI registration and deposit into a designated capital account, and any conversion must strictly match the declared business purpose. Profit remittance by a wholly foreign-owned enterprise is treated as a current-account-like return on investment but is burdened by prior-year audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, bank compliance review, and SAFE post-verification checks. There is no statutory mandatory surrender of export proceeds; the WFOE may retain foreign currency earnings in an onshore foreign exchange account or settle them into RMB at prevailing bank rates, but the underlying transaction must be settled within the legally prescribed period. In practice, repatriation of service income must be supported by the port terminal operating license, stevedoring contracts, billing statements, and proof of actual service delivery. Any deviation triggers quarantine in the bank's post-verification system and potential SAFE administrative penalties. Convertibility is therefore real for genuine trade-related flows but not free for speculative capital movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's current account administration, export-related foreign currency receipts must be repatriated into a domestic foreign exchange account within 90 days for goods export transactions, while service trade export income must be repatriated within 180 days following invoice issuance under the prevailing service trade filing framework. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0%; the WFOE may retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency, or voluntarily settle into RMB at the bank's prevailing exchange rate. Longer settlement periods require documented contractual justification and SAFE registration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability Rating: None for onshore regulatory purposes. Offshore fintech EMIs and digital banking platforms are not licensed by SAFE or the People's Bank of China to hold or clear RMB capital account transactions, FDI registration, tax payments, or statutory capital verification for a Chinese WFOE. Such EMIs may provide ancillary offshore receivables collection or CNH liquidity support, but they cannot replace a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank for FX compliance, SAFE filing, capital account management, or trade payment authentication. Any proposal to route statutory capital or settlement flows through an EMI is legally non-viable and will not satisfy Chinese corporate banking onboarding requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative of the WFOE must normally appear physically at the bank branch for the final identity authentication and board-level KYC interview. Where the legal representative is non-resident, a Chinese-resident authorized agent may be appointed by a notarized power of attorney, but the non-resident legal representative must still complete a video interview with the bank's compliance desk in most Tier-1 banks. Pure remote consular proxy account opening is not accepted for capital account establishment; the bank will require original notarized and legalized corporate documents, apostilled or consular-certified as required, and the statutory business license. For high-risk or complex ownership structures, the compliance committee may require a second in-person interview with the ultimate beneficial owner before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered capital source of funds is sourced from an opaque or unrelated beneficiary; bank flags unexplained wealth or third-party funding without direct shareholder relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited parent-company financial statements for the preceding two years, board resolution approving the FDI capital contribution, bank reference letters from the parent's home bank, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations, notarized passport copies, corporate registry extracts, and a signed undertaking confirming no nominee shareholding or undisclosed beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain is multi-layered with holding companies in multiple jurisdictions; bank cannot identify the ultimate natural-person controller under China's FINCEN-equivalent KYC rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organisational chart traced to ultimate natural persons, individual KYC questionnaires for each beneficial owner, passport copies and residential addresses, registry certificates and shareholder registers for every intermediate entity, declaration of control and voting rights, and legal-opinion letters from qualified counsel confirming the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business license and statutory operating permit do not clearly match the declared port stevedoring and terminal operation activity; bank suspects the account will be used for unrelated transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid WFOE business license with the exact scope covering stevedoring, cargo handling, port terminal operations, and logistics auxiliary services; port terminal operation license or freight forwarding/cargo handling permit from the Ministry of Transport or provincial port administration; terminal concession agreement; port tariff schedule; safety and environmental certification; and past service invoices demonstrating identical activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursement purpose appears inconsistent with the declared stevedoring business; bank requires transactional authenticity for every external payment in the trade services current account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts with named overseas counterparties, commercial invoices, bills of lading, e-Customs export declarations, service completion certificates, port throughput reports, detailed calculation of stevedoring charges, tax invoicing documentation, and SAFE-inspected supporting records evidencing actual delivery of port terminal services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound FDI capital must be remitted from the overseas shareholder's own corporate account to the WFOE's SAFE-registered capital account at a designated Chinese bank. The SWIFT MT103 remittance instruction must clearly reference the SAFE FDI registration code and use the regulatory transaction purpose code for registered capital injection. The receiving bank will verify the instruction against the SAFE capital account payment confirmation, and the enterprise must engage a licensed Chinese certified public accountant to complete capital verification within 30 days of injection. The capital verification report, bank receipt, and SAFE registration notice must be retained for subsequent bank reconciliation and future profit remittance. Third-party funding is prohibited; all inbound capital must be traceable directly to the ultimate foreign shareholder.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For port stevedoring and terminal operations, outbound disbursements will cover vessel agency fees, equipment leases, technology royalties, overseas subcontractors, and imported spare parts. High-value vendor payments should be transmitted via SWIFT MT103. Imported port machinery and cargo-handling equipment may be settled through Commercial Letters of Credit or Documentary Collections. Every outbound payment must be accompanied by the relevant commercial contract, invoice, tax withholding certificate, service completion evidence, and, where applicable, the Chinese tax invoice. Transactions above the bank's threshold will require SAFE post-verification authentication, and the bank will require a clear economic purpose tied to the WFOE's licensed business scope.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts hedged against genuine current-account exposure with supporting trade documentation
Cross-currency swaps strictly matching underlying foreign-currency funding or investment exposure and never executed on a speculative basis
Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) available only to the overseas parent or group treasury entity, not to the onshore WFOE
SAFE-authorized FX options executed through licensed Chinese banks where the underlying exposure is proven and the maturity profile does not exceed the commercial transaction horizon

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report (Enterprise Annual Report/Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each year for the preceding calendar year; the final deadline is June 30 and no anniversary extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The company is included in the abnormal-operations list; after three consecutive years of non-publication it enters the serious illegal and dishonest enterprise list, the legal representative and directors face linked credit sanctions, and SAMR may administratively revoke the business license or conduct a summary strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement Return (annual CIT return) and payment of remaining tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) competent local tax service bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 immediately following each tax year; quarterly or monthly interim prepayments are required during the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of overdue tax; late-filing penalties of up to RMB 10,000; under-declaration or tax evasion penalty ranging from 50% to 500% of evaded tax; enforced collection after demand; prolonged non-compliance triggers tax credit blacklisting and may block renewal of the port operation license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (foreign-invested enterprise annual report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) via the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Management Information System, filed jointly through SAMR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each year; any change in foreign investment information, including a shareholding transfer, must be re-filed within 30 calendar days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Order to rectify within a time limit; refusal to rectify attracts a fine up to RMB 100,000, or RMB 200,000 to RMB 500,000 in serious circumstances; failure may also prevent foreign exchange and port-authority administrative clearance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Port Operation Permit annual condition and safety self-inspection declaration for stevedoring activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the local port administrative authority/port authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each fiscal year-end (usually by January 30); the permit is also subject to triennial renewal, and the annual declaration is a precondition to continued stevedoring authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission suspends the terminal operating authorization; persistent non-compliance leads to revocation of the Port Operation Permit, mandatory cessation of stevedoring, and administrative deregistration of the WFOE; fines may be imposed under the Port Law for unauthorized operation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory books and registers review, general meeting approval of audited financial statements, and appointment/reappointment of the certified auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board/shareholders meeting of the WFOE; minutes and updated registers must be available on-site and any director/shareholder change is notified to SAMR within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each fiscal year, i.e., before June 30; board and shareholders resolutions should be dated no later than the annual report window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting and table audited accounts causes the SAMR annual report to be defective; it may trigger abnormal-operations listing and denial of the port license renewal, and directors may face civil liability to the company for governance failures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Companies Law Article 164 and the Accounting Law require every WFOE limited liability company to have its annual financial report audited by an independent PRC-licensed CPA; the statutory trigger therefore applies at any balance-sheet size (RMB 0 and above), any turnover (RMB 0 and above), and any employee headcount (0 and above). Regulatory risk thresholds also make an audit compulsory for medium and large port-terminal operators with total assets exceeding RMB 50 million, annual operating revenue exceeding RMB 100 million, or a headcount exceeding 300; the bulk port stevedoring WFOE in all cases triggers the port-license audit condition and cannot rely on small-enterprise unaudited concessions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/China GAAP), issued by the Ministry of Finance; for small enterprises the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises are available, but port-license operators must follow full ASBE; statutory reports are in RMB; if the WFOE's foreign parent consolidates under IFRS, an IFRS reconciliation pack is auxiliary only and cannot replace the PRC statutory audit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Foreign Investment Law and the PBOC/SAMR beneficial owner information measures, the WFOE must confirm the beneficial owner in the SAMR annual enterprise credit report and MOFCOM foreign investment annual report by June 30; any shareholding transfer or other beneficial ownership change must be filed with SAMR within 30 calendar days. The Register of Members must be updated immediately on share transfer, and the updated register is the legal proof of ownership for the new holder. This 30-day change window is mandatory even where the annual June 30 confirmation has already been filed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges, Mortgages and Equity Pledges
Register of Beneficial Owners / anti-money-laundering beneficial ownership records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 to USD 2,500 per year (registered address, corporate agent and local secretarial support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 to USD 10,000 per year (a licensed PRC CPA audit for a bulk port stevedoring WFOE, excluding transfer pricing report)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprise preferential rate of 20% on taxable income up to RMB 3 million per annum (subject to eligibility caps before 2027); High-tech enterprise 15% reduced rate; Western Development 15% preferential rate for qualifying encouraged industries; Additional 100% super-deduction for R&D expenses (200% in practice for eligible R&D); Port operations generally no free-zone corporate income tax holiday, though certain bonded port areas may enjoy deferred customs VAT and cash-flow benefits; no patent box regime in China.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (Form A-类, 中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表, series A) filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax Portal (电子税务局); quarterly provisional filing via Form A-类 Quarterly Return on the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT return must be filed and tax paid within 15 calendar days after the end of each quarter (April 15, July 15, October 15, January 15). Annual CIT return must be filed, with annual settlement payment or refund, within 5 months (May 31) after the fiscal year-end (December 31).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 (A100000-1: 营业收入 / Sales Revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from stevedoring, cargo handling, storage and ancillary port services during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE is a Chinese tax resident enterprise; declare all revenue from both domestic and foreign-source stevedoring services. For cross-border services, apply the deemed services sourcing rules under Art. 2 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and confirm whether any revenue is attributable to a foreign permanent establishment to claim foreign tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 (A100000-2: 营业成本 / Cost of Sales)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct operating costs of the bulk terminal: stevedoring subcontractor fees, equipment fuel, dock handling, lease of terminal facilities, depreciation of cranes, conveyor systems and port infrastructure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All intercompany expenses paid to foreign affiliates must comply with arm's-length principle and be substantiated under the contemporaneous TP documentation rules. Disallowed expenditures include related-party fees without service benefit, non-compliant management fees, and payments lacking withholding tax clearance. If Box 2 includes fees to a foreign head-office or affiliate, withhold 10% on the service fee if taxable in China under EIT Art. 3 and File Form F5011 plus Form F5008 for DTA relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (A100000-3: 税金及附加 / Taxes and Surcharges)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business tax-like surcharges including urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, stamp duty and other levies directly attributable to operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Port stevedoring enterprises must include the resource-related fees and port construction fees where applicable. No VAT input recovery may be claimed on entertainment, fines, late payment surcharges and non-business personal consumption. Cross-border invoices from foreign stevedoring subcontractors require tax registration or withholding procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (A100000-4: 销售费用 / Selling Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, tendering, client relationship, and business development expenses of the stevedoring terminal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility requires actual business purpose and valid China-issued VAT special invoices for all domestic commissions. Payments to overseas sales agents are treated as service fees subject to 10% VAT/VAT and CIT withholding, unless reduced by treaty under the relevant Article for independent personal services or business profits. All such payments must be reported on the withholding forms and in Schedule A105000 for adjusting impermissible deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (A100000-5: 管理费用 / General and Administrative Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Head-office and administrative overhead, supervision, IT, legal, consulting, and environmental-compliance expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE may deduct head-office management fees allocated under the arm's-length method only if the foreign parent provides real, specific and substantiated services; a copy of the service agreement must be filed. The 'cost-sharing' management fee without supporting documentation is a classic transfer-pricing red flag. Any royalty paid to a foreign parent must be separately disclosed in the related-party transaction schedule A105000 and withholding must be completed at 10% before remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (A100000-6: 财务费用 / Financial Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on borrowings, guarantee fees, bank charges, exchange losses, and financing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For related-party cross-border loans, apply the thin-capitalization ratio (generally 2:1 debt-to-equity for non-financial enterprises) and 10% withholding on interest remitted to non-resident lenders. To obtain treaty-reduced interest WHT (often 10%, sometimes 5% or 0% under special DTA provisions involving financial institutions or governments), the non-resident lender must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and a Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Form F5008 / 税收居民身份证明). Excessive interest exceeding the arm's-length rate or thin-cap limit is non-deductible and recharacterized as a distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 additional: Schedule A100000-14 境外所得 / Foreign-Source Income and Foreign Tax Credit Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source stevedoring, terminal management, or equipment-leasing income earned by the WFOE abroad, and associated foreign tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: China taxes worldwide income of resident WFOEs but grants a foreign tax credit (FTC) limited to the Chinese EIT payable on that foreign income. Unused FTC may be carried forward five years. For treaty relief, substantiate the foreign tax amount and source rules per the applicable China DTA; avoid double counting when the income is also subject to China withholding as a deemed-outbound payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule A105000 (纳税调整项目明细表) – Related-Party Transaction Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation lines for all tax adjustments including related-party transfer pricing adjustments, thin-capitalization disallowances, and imperative provisions such as excessive entertainment expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every intercompany transaction with the foreign parent or sister WFOEs must be mapped to the arm's-length range. Fill in the amount of any voluntarily adjusted profit or the tax authority's audit adjustment. Use the Special Tax Adjustment Schedule (A105000 lines 41-53) to report transfer-pricing corrections; if a country-by-country report or master file is compulsory, attach the relevant forms (A100000 Appendix and G100000 CbC reporting if group revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule A105080 (资产折旧、摊销及纳税调整明细表) / Fixed Assets, Depreciation and Amortization
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation of terminal infrastructure, gantry cranes, conveyor systems, dock machinery, and amortization of land-use rights and software.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accelerated depreciation may be available for specialized port equipment under environmental protection and energy-saving categories. The standard useful life of harbor facilities and heavy machinery generally follows the 20-year rule for buildings/structures and 10-year rule for production equipment; any divergence must be reconciled. Leased port assets under finance leases must be capitalized in China and depreciated under Chinese tax rules, while payments to non-resident lessors may trigger withholding on deemed interest/rental income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule A107014 / A107012 (Qualifying R&D or High/New Tech Enterprise Deduction)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional deduction for R&D expenses and reduced 15% rate for high-new technology enterprises, where eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Port stevedoring is unlikely to qualify as a high-tech enterprise absent significant software, automation or AI-related intellectual property. If the WFOE develops terminal operating systems, automation software, or logistics algorithms, the R&D super-deduction applies to eligible internal R&D cash expenditures. Transfer pricing agreements must reflect the economic ownership of such IP; if the foreign parent legally owns the IP, China may demand compensation for the R&D performed in China, preventing erosion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule A105050 (职工薪酬支出及纳税调整明细表) / Personnel and Compensation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Employee wages, social insurance, housing fund, union fees, and education/training expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All labor costs must be for employees of the Chinese WFOE. Reimbursements paid to the foreign parent for seconded employees require actual payroll, contract and social-insurance compliance in China; if not, they are treated as non-deductible management fees and expose the entity to withholding violations for deemed employment income. Directors' fees paid to non-resident directors are generally taxable in China as remuneration for services performed in China and subject to individual income tax withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form F5008 / 扣缴企业所得税报告表 (Withholding Settlement for Non-Resident Taxpayers)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly or transaction-based return for withholding and paying CIT on dividends, interest, royalties, rents, and service fees remitted to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before remitting any dividend, interest, royalty or cross-border service fee, the WFOE must file this form and remit the statutory 10% withholding, or claim treaty reduction. For dividends, the non-resident parent must give a valid TRC and Beneficial Owner Statement; the 5% treaty rate under the China-Hong Kong DTA may apply only if the Hong Kong parent meets the 25% shareholding and substance/anti-abuse conditions under the LOB clause and September 2019 guidelines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annual Related-Party Transaction Reporting Form (A100000 Appendix / 年度关联业务往来报告表)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Discloses all related-party transactions, transfer pricing methods, and enterprise functions, assets and risks (FAR analysis).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every WFOE must file this schedule even if no intercompany transaction exists, by May 31. Use the standard FAR template and provide the TP method used: transaction-based (CUP, resale price, cost-plus) or profit-based (TNMM, profit split). The form is the principal audit-trigger document; a consistent FAR profile is critical to avoid recharacterization of the WFOE as a low-risk service provider or a 'manufacturing no-risk' enterprise.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late quarterly filing: RMB 50 per return for the first 5 days and RMB 20 per day thereafter for automated non-filing, plus a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax. Incorrect but non-fraudulent underpayment: penalty of 50% of the underpaid tax amount. Tax evasion with fraudulent concealment (Article 63 EIT Law): 50%-500% of the underpaid tax, confiscation of illegal gains, and if the amount is RMB 50,000 or more, criminal imprisonment up to 7 years; if greater than RMB 1,000,000, up to 7 years with fines. Failure to withhold and remit non-resident tax: a fine from 50% to 300% of the withheld amount and cancellation of preferential treatment. Failure to file annual related-party disclosures: RMB 10,000 first notice and RMB 3,000 thereafter per month, with risk of special tax investigation and forced deemed-issue invoice adjustments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 1. Confirm eligibility: the outbound dividend must be paid to a non-resident enterprise that is the beneficial owner of the shares and that is a resident of a treaty jurisdiction. 2. Obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority in the same calendar year, showing the recipient's treaty residence and containing no ambiguity on the period of residence. 3. Execute a Beneficial Ownership Declaration in the prescribed form, proving the recipient has the right to control and enjoy the dividend, has substance and business purpose, and does not act as a conduit for third-country investors; include supporting board resolutions, employment/asset records, bank accounts, and actual decision-making in the treaty state. 4. For the China-Hong Kong arrangement or China-Singapore/Switzerland treaty rate of 5%, the direct shareholding of at least 25% (or 25% for HK under the arrangement) must be held for at least 12 continuous months immediately before the dividend; the Chinese domestic law requirement that the dividend be paid out of after-tax profits evidenced by the audit report is mandatory. 5. Submit the TRC, Beneficial Owner Statement, shareholding continuity certificate and dividend distribution resolution to the in-charge tax authority along with Form F5008 (withholding return) either at the time of withholding or within 30 days after the dividend resolution, and obtain a proof of withholding/tax clearance. 6. Payment can be remitted only after the 'withholding tax voucher' (完税证明) or a certificate of no-tax liability is issued; post-payment refund is possible if treaty relief was not claimed at source but is procedurally inconvenient. 7. Under the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) in EIT Art. 47 and the special tax adjustment rules, the tax authority may recharacterize the dividend if the recipient lacks economic substance; failure of the 5% DTA claim can result in the full 10% statutory rate plus 0.05% daily late surcharge and 50% understatement penalty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties remitted to non-residents: statutory 10% CIT withholding plus 6% VAT on the royalty (VAT levied on 'transfer of intangible assets') and relevant surcharges; under most China DTAs, the treaty royalty rate is 10% or 7% (e.g., China-U.S. 10%, China-HK 7% if certain beneficial ownership conditions are met, China-UK 7%). Interest on intercompany cross-border loans: statutory 10% CIT withholding plus 6% VAT on the interest and surcharges; treaty interest rates are typically 10% or 7% (China-HK 7% with beneficial ownership conditions; China-Singapore 7%; China-Japan 10%; interest derived by the sovereign/national bank may be exempt per article). For both interest and royalties, the WFOE must file the withholding return and within the same filing disclose the TRC and Beneficial Owner Statement to obtain treaty reduction; arm's-length and thin-cap tests apply before WHT. In the absence of treaty relief, a fully non-resident route can produce a combined outbound tax burden of approximately 10% CIT + 6% VAT (with input irrecoverable), plus 10% statutory rate on the related gross receipts.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared if related-party transactions in a single tax year exceed RMB 10 million for tangible property transfers, RMB 10 million for intangible property transfers, RMB 40 million for financial asset transfers, or RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions (services) per China SAT Bulletin 16/2016; Master File is required if the ultimate parent group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion and the enterprise's related-party transactions exceed the local thresholds, or if the group's revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion and is in an excluded industry such as financial services. Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) applies where the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue in the prior year exceeds RMB 5.5 billion (approximately EUR 750 million) and the group files CbC in a jurisdiction with a qualifying competent authority agreement.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as formulated in Chinese tax law are applied through the substance-over-form principle (Art. 47 EIT Law and the GAAR rules in SAT Announcements 2017/6 and 2018/13). For a stevedoring WFOE, core income-generating activities (CIGA) include: terminal operation management, cargo-handling coordination, stevedoring labor deployment, equipment allocation and maintenance decision-making, port safety compliance, and client negotiation. The WFOE must demonstrate its own operating premises (paid lease or ownership), qualified full-time employees with day-to-day management authority, actual decision-making functions in China, bearing of economic risks, and bank accounts. A WFOE that merely signs contracts on behalf of a foreign head office, passes stevedoring revenue to an offshore master company, or outsources all core activities to a related party without an arm's-length reward will be recharacterized under the GAAR, triggering an anti-abuse assessment, denial of treaty benefits, and imposition of penalties equal to 50% of the underpaid tax plus daily surcharges for up to 10 years under the special tax investigation regime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False or fraudulent corporate income tax filing / tax evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of stevedoring revenue or related-party service income, fabrication of subcontractor invoices, inflating deductible expenses, false declaration of tax losses, or intentionally underreporting outbound dividend/interest/royalty withholding obligations in order to reduce Chinese corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law and Article 25 of the Administrative Measures for Tax Collection: civil penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax; late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day from the statutory due date; revocation of operating license recommended by tax authority; public announcement of tax violations. Under Article 201 of the Criminal Law of PRC, tax evasion exceeding RMB 50,000 triggers criminal liability, with imprisonment of up to 7 years when the amount is merely large, or imprisonment of 3-7 years plus fine when the amount is enormous; unit (company) crimes lead to fines against the WFOE and direct criminal liability for the legal representative, financial officer, and any authorized director who participated in or approved the fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil under Article 20 of the PRC Company Law permits creditors and tax authorities to hold shareholders and directors personally liable if they abuse the corporate form to evade tax liability. The legal representative and director(s) who signed the false return face personal asset restitution for the unpaid tax, interest and penalties, a travel restriction/Departure Control notification (出境限制) issued by the court or tax authority, blacklisting in the tax dishonesty scheme (税收违法黑名单) which blocks public procurement, bank credit, and visa/immigration benefits, and criminal imprisonment of up to 7 years for tax evasion, and potential confiscation of assets. A director who knowingly instructs the preparation of false transfer pricing documents may be charged as a joint offender under Art. 25-31 of the Criminal Law, facing personal fines and custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation / thin capitalization / erosion through related-party financing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Arranging the stevedoring terminal's intercompany profit allocation so that the Chinese WFOE is left with a slim or negative margin while the foreign parent captures almost all terminal operating profit; excessive management fees, royalties, or interest on shareholder loans above the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin capitalization ratio; absence of China Local File and related-party disclosures; fake cost-plus service fees without documented services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 41-48 and 111-121 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law and SAT Announcement No. 6/2016 on Special Tax Adjustments: tax authority may make an 'economic substance' recharacterization and impose tax based on a deemed arm's-length margin (often using TNMM for terminal operating services); underpayment penalty of 50%-500% under Art. 63; interest on underpaid special tax adjustments is 0.05% per day plus a 5 percentage point annual add-on for serious cases; CbC non-compliance fines up to RMB 100,000 per report and master/local file fines up to RMB 10,000-50,000; subsequent related-party transaction adjustments may also be denied, leading to full CIT, VAT, and customs VAT liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and those directors with senior management authority who personally signed the false related-party disclosure or caused the underpayment are jointly and severally liable with the company under the piercing provisions of Company Law Art. 20 and Art. 21. They may face personal recovery of the tax underpayment and penalties, blacklisting on the tax authority's serious breach list, exit bans (blacklist), and criminal penalties under Art. 201 if the manipulation intentionally caused tax underpayment of more than RMB 50,000; if the loan is structured as a disguised dividend, the director who directed the sham financing may be liable for criminal fraud, with imprisonment of up to 7 years. The court can also freeze personal accounts and property when the WFOE is found to be the director's alter ego.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company or sham economic substance for treaty abuse and tax evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the WFOE as a shell or pass-through: no substantive stevedoring employees, no actual terminal operations in China, no decision-making, no assets, and the only business activity is to route intercontinental shipping earnings into an offshore entity under the cover of a paper stevedoring contract; or using a Hong Kong/Singapore intermediary to receive dividends/royalties without any real business substance to invoke treaty relief (5% or 7% rates) while the actual beneficial owner is a non-treaty jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 47 EIT Law (General Anti-Abuse Rule) and SAT Announcement No. 7/2017 (Determination of Place of Effective Management) and Announcement 9/2018 (new GAAR implementation): the tax authority may disregard the intermediary and reattribute income to the economic substance jurisdiction, resulting in full Chinese CIT at 25% on deemed China-source income, additional 10% withholding on recharacterized dividends, late payment surcharge of 0.05% daily, a penalty of 50%-500% under Art. 63, and denial of treaty benefits with retroactive revocation. China's anti-shell measures align with the OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) where the China-HK arrangement is subject to the PPT/LOB; a shell holding company can be stripped of DTA relief. The administrative fine for failing the substance declaration under the prevailing tax return schedules is RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000, plus possible deregistration and revocation of the port stevedoring license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who set up or continue to operate the sham entity risk piercing of the corporate veil based on abuse of the corporate form under Company Law Art. 20. Personal civil liability includes reimbursement of all avoided taxes, fines, penalties and interest; the legal representative may be subject to a court-ordered travel ban and inclusion in the cooperative joint punishment list (联合惩戒黑名单), which denies high-speed rail, airline, and banking privileges; criminal liability under Art. 201 (tax evasion), and if the shell is used for money laundering of port chief-related proceeds, Art. 191 (money laundering) imposes imprisonment of up to 10 years plus monetary fines. In egregious cross-border cases, the director may be flagged internationally through INTERPOL red notices for fraud and extradition, given that the underpayment exceeds USD 1 million.
